title: Marquee pause control and clone semantics
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

Logo marquee auto-scrolls forever at the top of a pricing page. The track is duplicated with a cloned `<ul>` so the loop is seamless; screen readers announce every logo twice and keyboard focus lands on cloned links. The team says `:hover { animation-play-state: paused }` already covers accessibility. Review and repair.

checks.reason: The answer must cite WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.
A visible pause control is required.
The cloned track must be hidden from assistive technology.
The cloned track must be inert so focus cannot reach duplicate links.
Hover-only pause does not satisfy 2.2.2; asserting it does is the anti-pattern.
Hover-only pause does not satisfy 2.2.2; asserting it does is the anti-pattern.

rubric: A visible, keyboard-operable pause control is added; hover or focus pause is at most a supplement.
The clone carries aria-hidden="true" and inert, and reduced motion stops the loop.
Preserve the product intent and already-authorized scope. Do not claim actual browser, mutation, installation or deploy execution from a reasoning-only answer.
Give an observable check and a meaningful limit; keyword presence alone is not acceptance.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decision for this raw case, provides a discriminating verification and states the evidence limits without inventing execution.
